title: Mahindra XEV 9S Bharat NCAP: 5 Stars, 76.15 Points | Skill-Lync
summary: XEV 9S Bharat NCAP result: 31.15/32 adult, 45/49 child, 5 stars. Official scores, where it lost points, 3-row SUV comparison, what it means for engineers.
body_markdown:
The Mahindra XEV 9S, a three-row electric SUV, has a 5-star Bharat NCAP rating for both adult and child occupant protection. Its official scores are **31.15 out of 32** (adult) and **45 out of 49** (child). Mahindra announced the result in Mumbai on 17 November 2026, and the rating is listed on the Bharat NCAP portal as applying from November 2026. Mahindra says it is the first 7-seat EV in India to get 5 stars.


- **Adult score 31.15/32:** 15.15/16 in the 64 km/h frontal offset test, a full 16/16 in the 50 km/h side barrier test, and a pass in the side pole test (Bharat NCAP fact sheet).
- **Child score 45/49:** full marks in the dynamic dummy tests (24/24) and for child-seat installation (12/12), and 9/13 on the vehicle-based checks.
- **Test car:** 79 kWh Pack Two Above (6-seat) and Pack Three Above (7-seat) variants, crash-test weight 2,529 kg, assessed in July 2026.
- **Third INGLO-platform 5-star:** it follows the XEV 9e and BE 6, both rated in January 2025.


## What did Bharat NCAP give the XEV 9S?


The XEV 9S got 5 stars in both categories. It scored 31.15/32 for adult occupants and 45/49 for children. Its only adult points went in the frontal offset crash (0.85 points). On the child side it dropped all 4 points in the vehicle-based checks, which look at features rather than crash readings.


The fact sheet lists ISOFIX mounts on the second-row outboard seats only, no integrated child seat, and a manual passenger-airbag cut-off switch. The driver's knee airbag is listed as "No – optional". Stability control, curtain airbags, pedestrian protection and seat-belt reminders are standard on every variant.


Of the 81 points available, the XEV 9S dropped 0.85 in the frontal test and 4 in the vehicle-based child checks. Data: Bharat NCAP fact sheet, read 18 Nov 2026.


## Is the XEV 9S really the safest 7-seater in India?


Mahindra calls it the highest-scoring 7-seater Bharat NCAP has tested, with a combined 76.15 points. Bharat NCAP itself publishes stars and two separate scores, not a combined total, so "safest" is Mahindra's framing. Of the three-row SUVs we checked on the official portal, the XEV 9S does have the highest adult and child scores:


Three-row SUV Adult /32 Child /49 Sum Crash-test weight


Mahindra XEV 9S (EV, assessed Jul 2026) 31.15 45.00 76.15 2,529 kg


Mahindra XUV 7XO (assessed Jul 2026) 30.76 44.97 75.73 2,059 kg


Tata Safari (rated from Dec 2023) 30.08 44.54 74.62 2,126 kg


The gaps are small, and all three clear the 27-point adult and 41-point child thresholds for 5 stars. Our[tracker of every 2026 Bharat NCAP result](https://skill-lync.com/blogs/bharat-ncap-ratings-2026) explains how those thresholds work.


## Why does this matter for engineers?


Weight is what makes this result interesting. In the frontal test, the car drives into a fixed deformable barrier, so the structure has to absorb the car's own kinetic energy. At 64 km/h (17.78 m/s):

The 2,059 kg XUV 7XO brings about 325 kJ to the same test. So the XEV 9S crumple zone has to manage roughly 23% more energy, with a large battery pack under the floor that must not be crushed or punctured. The side barrier test works the other way. A 950 kg trolley hits a stationary car, so a heavier car gets pushed less. In an idealised plastic collision, the XEV 9S picks up about 13.7 km/h, against 15.8 km/h for the XUV 7XO. For a heavy EV, the frontal test is the harder one, and that is where the XEV 9S lost its 0.85 adult points.


Results like this come out of many rounds of crash simulation run before a car ever reaches a test agency. In India that work employs crash CAE engineers (LS-DYNA, Radioss and HyperMesh), restraint-system engineers who tune airbags and pretensioners, battery-pack structural engineers, and homologation engineers who work through AIS-197, the standard Bharat NCAP runs on.


## What happens next?


The rating covers the variants in the fact sheet's annexure: One Above, Two Above, Three and Three Above trims with 59, 70 and 79 kWh packs, in 6- and 7-seat form. There are no Three trims on the 70 kWh pack. If you are buying, check that your exact variant is listed. Students can read the 4-page[official fact sheet](https://www.bncap.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/FACT-SHEET_XEV-9S.pdf) to see what a crash-test report records.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the Mahindra XEV 9S Bharat NCAP rating?


5 stars for adult occupant protection (31.15/32) and 5 stars for child occupant protection (45/49). The car was assessed in July 2026, and the rating applies from November 2026.


### Is the XEV 9S the first 7-seater EV with 5 stars in Bharat NCAP?


That is Mahindra's claim, made in its 17 November 2026 release. Bharat NCAP publishes ratings car by car and does not rank cars or label firsts.


### Where did the XEV 9S lose points?


It dropped 0.85 points in the frontal offset test and 4 of 13 points in the vehicle-based child checks. It scored full marks in the side barrier, child dynamic and child-seat installation tests.
